mainTopic: Why offering loaves baked for oneself do not work for the מצוה of מצה: the sources of רבה and רב יוסף, why simpler sources do not suffice, and why loaves baked for the market do work.
overview: The משנה taught that חלות תודה and רקיקי נזיר baked for one's own offering cannot be used for the מצוה of מצה on פסח. רבה learns this from "וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם אֶת הַמַּצּוֹת": the מצה must be guarded for the sake of מצה, and these loaves were guarded for a זבח. רב יוסף learns it from "שִׁבְעַת יָמִים מַצּוֹת תֹּאכֵלוּ": the מצה must be fit to eat all seven days, and these loaves may be eaten only for a day and a night. A ברייתא supports each view. The גמרא then asks why simpler sources would not already exclude these loaves. It suggests three: לחם עני read as food fit for אנינות, the rule against מצה עשירה, and the rule that מצה must be eaten בכל מושבותיכם. Each suggestion is answered, so the special verses are still needed. Finally, a ברייתא reports רבי יהושע's ruling that loaves baked to sell in the market do work for the מצוה. רבה explains why: the seller always planned to eat any unsold loaves as his own מצה.

steps.title: רבה's reason: מצה must be guarded for the sake of מצה
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that the verse "וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם אֶת הַמַּצּוֹת" requires מצה that was guarded for the purpose of מצה. Offering loaves were guarded for the purpose of a זבח, so they do not qualify.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And you shall guard the מצות" means מצה that was guarded for the sake of מצה. This excludes מצה that was not guarded for the sake of מצה, but for the sake of a זבח (sacrifice).
steps.whatsHappening: This continues רבה's answer to the גמרא's question of why חלות תודה and רקיקי נזיר cannot be used for the מצה obligation. He brings a פסוק showing the מצה must be guarded with the right intention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם" teaches that guarding the dough from becoming חמץ must be done with the goal of making מצה for the מצוה. Offering loaves were also guarded from becoming חמץ, but the purpose was the offering. For רבה, the problem is the intention behind the guarding.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall guard: the source for guarding the מצה
That is guarded, meaning watched so it does not become חמץ
For the sake of מצה, with the intention of the מצוה
This is excluded, a standard formula for what a פסוק rules out
A sacrifice

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying the loaves are חמץ or invalid as מצה. They were properly guarded from leavening. The only issue is the purpose: they were guarded for the offering rather than for the מצוה of מצה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic source for the idea of שימור לשם מצה, guarding the מצה with intent for the מצוה.

phrases.english: "And you shall guard the matzot"
phrases.notes: שמות יב:יז

phrases.english: means matza that is guarded for the sake of matza.

phrases.aramaic: יָצְתָה זוֹ שֶׁאֵין מִשְׁתַּמֶּרֶת לְשֵׁם מַצָּה,
phrases.english: This excludes this matza, which is not guarded for the sake of matza,
but for the sake of a sacrifice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבה's answer, whose attribution and the גמרא's question asking for the source came on the previous amud.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The loaves were guarded for a זבח, not for מצה, and the פסוק requires guarding for the sake of מצה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מצה must be guarded לשם מצה. Offering loaves are guarded לשם זבח and are excluded.

steps.title: רב יוסף's reason: מצה must be fit to eat all seven days
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף gives a different source: "שִׁבְעַת יָמִים מַצּוֹת תֹּאכֵלוּ" means the מצה must be the kind that can be eaten for all seven days. Offering loaves may be eaten only for a day and a night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: The פסוק says, "Seven days you shall eat מצות." This means מצה that can be eaten for seven days. This excludes מצה that cannot be eaten for seven days, but only for a day and a night.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף offers a second, different answer to the same question of why these loaves do not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב יוסף, the problem is not intention but the status of the food. חלות תודה and רקיקי נזיר are קדשים that must be eaten within a day and a night, after which they become נותר. The פסוק requires מצה whose type is fit for the whole festival.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק says, introducing a scriptural source
Seven days
That is eaten, meaning that may be eaten
For one day and one night, the time limit for eating these offerings

steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף does not mean you must actually eat this matza for all seven days. He means it must be the kind of matza that is allowed to be eaten for all seven days.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: The verse states:
"Seven days you shall eat matzot"
phrases.notes: שמות יב:טו

phrases.english: meaning matza that may be eaten for seven days.

phrases.aramaic: יָצְתָה זוֹ שֶׁאֵינָהּ נֶאֱכֶלֶת לְשִׁבְעַת יָמִים,
phrases.english: This excludes this matza, which may not be eaten for seven days,
but only for a day and a night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different פסוק and reason for the same ruling that רבה explained.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The loaves may be eaten only a day and a night, while the פסוק requires מצה that may be eaten all seven days.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מצה must be fit for eating all seven days. Offering loaves with a one-day limit are excluded.

steps.title: Each opinion has a supporting ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that there is a ברייתא supporting רבה and another ברייתא supporting רב יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא in accordance with רבה, and it was taught in a ברייתא in accordance with רב יוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא tells us it is about to quote two ברייתות, one backing each opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither view is rejected. Each one has support from a תנאי source, so both derivations stand.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
In accordance with him

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita in accordance with Rabba,

steps.title: The ברייתא supporting רבה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks whether one could fulfill the obligation with חלות תודה and רקיקי נזיר, and answers no, using "וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם אֶת הַמַּצּוֹת" exactly as רבה did.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in accordance with רבה: One might think a person can fulfill his obligation with חלות תודה or רקיקי נזיר. Therefore the פסוק says, "And you shall guard the מצות": מצה guarded for the sake of מצה. This excludes מצה that is not guarded for the sake of מצה, but for the sake of a זבח (sacrifice).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the first ברייתא, which uses רבה's exact פסוק and reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא starts with a possible mistaken assumption (יכול): perhaps offering loaves work, since they are real מצה. It then uses the פסוק to reject that idea. Its wording matches רבה word for word, which shows his view has a תנאי source.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought, introducing a rejected assumption
His obligation
The מצה loaves brought with a thanks-offering
The thin מצה wafers a נזיר brings at the end of his נזירות
Therefore the פסוק teaches

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Rabba:
One might think that he fulfills his obligation

phrases.english: This excludes this matza, which is not guarded for the sake of matza,

steps.title: The ברייתא supporting רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא reaches the same conclusion from "שִׁבְעַת יָמִים מַצּוֹת תֹּאכֵלוּ", matching רב יוסף's reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in accordance with רב יוסף: One might think a person can fulfill his obligation with חלות תודה or רקיקי נזיר. Therefore the פסוק says, "Seven days you shall eat מצות": מצה that may be eaten for seven. This excludes מצה that may not be eaten for seven, but only for a day and a night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the second ברייתא, which uses רב יוסף's פסוק and logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is the same as in the first ברייתא; only the source differs. Because both derivations have ברייתא support, the גמרא leaves both reasons standing.

keyTerms.meaning: For seven days, a shortened form of לשבעת ימים

steps.whatToRemember: Offering loaves baked for oneself do not work for מצה on פסח. רבה says it is because they were guarded for a זבח and not for מצה. רב יוסף says it is because they may be eaten only a day and a night, not all seven days. Each view has a ברייתא supporting it.

steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא using the same פסוק and reasoning

steps.title: Why not learn it from the words 'bread of affliction'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges both רבה and רב יוסף. Why not learn the rule from לחם עני, which according to one view means מצה must be food that may be eaten during אנינות? Offering loaves may not be eaten by an אונן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him learn it from 'bread of affliction' (לחם עני). This means bread that may be eaten while in אנינות. That excludes this bread, which is not eaten in אנינות but only in joy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks: why did רבה and רב יוסף need their own verses? There seems to be an easier source, the phrase לחם עני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a view that לחם עני means 'bread that can be eaten in a state of אנינות', meaning by a mourner on the day a close relative died. An אונן may not eat קדשים, so חלות תודה and רקיקי נזיר could never be eaten in אנינות. That would already exclude them, so why look for another verse?

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let him derive it' — the גמרא suggests a different, seemingly simpler source
'Bread of affliction' — the תורה's description of מצה (דברים ט״ז:ג)
The state of a mourner on the day a close relative dies, before burial; such a person may not eat קדשים
Joy — קדשים must be eaten in a state of joy, not mourning

steps.confusionAlert: The word עֹנִי here is not explained as 'poor'. In this reading it comes from אנינות, mourning. That is why it can exclude קדשים.

phrases.english: But let him derive it from 'bread of affliction' —
phrases.notes: The challenge is aimed at both רבה and רב יוסף

phrases.english: meaning bread that may be eaten in a state of acute mourning.
phrases.notes: Reading עֹנִי as connected to אנינות

phrases.english: This excludes this bread, which is not eaten in acute mourning,
phrases.notes: Offering loaves are קדשים, which an אונן may not eat

phrases.english: but only in joy!
phrases.notes: קדשים are eaten only in a state of שמחה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the derivations of רבה and רב יוסף were needed at all
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of verses by רבה (ושמרתם) and רב יוסף (שבעת ימים)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A simpler source, לחם עני read as 'bread fit for אנינות', already excludes offering loaves, so their verses seem unnecessary

steps.title: They hold like רבי עקיבא, who reads the word as 'poor'
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף follow רבי עקיבא. He reads the word as עָנִי, 'poor', not as related to אנינות. So for them לחם עני does not exclude offering loaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי עקיבא, who said: it is written עָנִי ('poor').
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבה and רב יוסף do not accept the 'mourning' reading of לחם עני. They follow רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא learns from how the word is written that it means 'poor bread', meaning plain, simple מצה. He does not read it as 'bread fit for אנינות'. So according to him, this phrase cannot exclude קדשים, and רבה and רב יוסף had to find other verses.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He holds like' — showing which earlier opinion an אמורא follows
The תנא who reads לחם עני as 'poor bread'
Poor — 'poor bread', meaning simple, plain מצה
'It is written' — a proof based on how the word is written in the תורה

phrases.english: He holds in accordance with Rabbi Akiva,
phrases.notes: Applies to both רבה and רב יוסף

phrases.english: who said that 'poor' is written.
phrases.notes: So the phrase teaches about 'poor bread', not about mourning

steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the אמוראים to a תנאי opinion that reads the verse differently
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought everyone reads לחם עני as 'bread fit for אנינות'
steps.terutzMaskana: רבה and רב יוסף follow רבי עקיבא, who reads it as 'poor bread', so it cannot exclude קדשים

steps.title: Why not exclude them because they are enriched מצה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks another question. Offering loaves contain oil, so they should count as מצה עשירה, which cannot be used for the מצוה anyway. Why were new verses needed?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him derive it from the fact that it is enriched מצה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second simpler reason. These loaves have oil in them, which should make them מצה עשירה, and that is already not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מצה for the מצוה must be plain 'poor bread', made only from flour and water. רבי עקיבא's reading of עני teaches exactly this. Since חלות תודה and רקיקי נזיר are made with oil, they should already be excluded for that reason. So again, why bring ושמרתם or שבעת ימים?

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rich' or enriched מצה — made with oil, wine, honey or other liquids besides water; not valid for the מצוה
'Since it is' — introduces the reason in the question

steps.whyThisMatters: This question ties back to רבי עקיבא from step 7. His 'poor bread' rule is the very rule that excludes מצה עשירה, so the question follows naturally.

phrases.english: But let him derive it
phrases.notes: Same formula as step 6: a simpler source is proposed

phrases.english: from the fact that it is enriched matza!
phrases.notes: These loaves are made with oil

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִיפּוֹק לֵיהּ דְּהָוֵה לֵיהּ מַצָּה עֲשִׁירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge of the same kind, now built on רבי עקיבא's 'poor bread' rule
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the verses of רבה and רב יוסף
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The oil in the loaves should make them מצה עשירה, which is already excluded, so no special verse is needed

steps.title: The oil is too little to make them enriched מצה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל בר רב יצחק answers that the oil is only a רביעית (a quarter of a לוג), divided among many loaves. Each loaf has so little oil that it is not מצה עשירה. So a separate verse is needed to exclude them.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל בר רב יצחק said: It is only a רביעית of oil, and it is divided among several loaves.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל בר רב יצחק answers the question from step 8. These loaves do not count as מצה עשירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The total oil is only a רביעית, and it is spread across several loaves. The amount in each loaf is too small to change its status, so it stays regular מצה. Since the 'poor bread' rule does not exclude these loaves, רבה and רב יוסף really did need their own verses.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarter of a לוג — a small measure of liquid
It is divided or spread out
Loaves

steps.whatToRemember: Offering loaves are not excluded by לחם עני. For רבי עקיבא that phrase is not about mourning, and the small amount of oil does not make them מצה עשירה. That is why רבה needs ושמרתם and רב יוסף needs שבעת ימים.

steps.terutzMaskana: The oil is only a רביעית spread over several loaves, too little to count as enriched, so a separate verse is needed

steps.title: Why not exclude offering loaves because they cannot be eaten everywhere?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we need special verses to exclude חלות תודה and רקיקי נזיר. These loaves can only be eaten in a holy place, and מצה must be food eaten 'בכל מושבותיכם' (in all your dwellings).
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him learn it from the fact that these loaves cannot be eaten in all dwelling places!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises another challenge. Offering loaves cannot be eaten everywhere, so they should already be disqualified from the מצוה of מצה without any new verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned that מצה must be food that can be eaten 'בכל מושבותיכם', anywhere in ארץ ישראל. Offering loaves may only be eaten in ירושלים. So this rule should already exclude them, and the special verses of רבה and רב יוסף seem unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And let him derive it' (from a different, simpler source)
'In all your dwellings': מצה must be food that can be eaten anywhere
The loaves that come with a thanksgiving offering
The thin wafers a נזיר brings at the end of his נזירות

phrases.english: And let him derive it
phrases.notes: A standard formula: 'you already have another source, so why the new one?'

phrases.english: from the fact that they are not eaten in all dwelling places!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִיפּוֹק לֵיהּ דְּאֵינָן נֶאֱכָלוֹת בְּכׇל מוֹשָׁבוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a third challenge in a row against the need for special verses, after the challenges from לחם עני and מצה עשירה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the special verses brought by רבה and רב יוסף to exclude offering loaves.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A general rule (בכל מושבותיכם) already excludes food that is limited to one place. So a dedicated verse should be unnecessary.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: These loaves were eaten in נוב and גבעון
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש infers from this reasoning not being used that חלות תודה and רקיקי נזיר could be eaten in נוב and גבעון. So they do count as food eaten 'in all dwellings'.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: This teaches that thanksgiving loaves and נזיר wafers are eaten in נוב and גבעון.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש explains why the 'all dwellings' reason does not work here. He also draws a new halachic fact from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the בית המקדש was built, there was a period when the משכן stood in נוב and in גבעון. Lighter offerings like these could then be eaten anywhere in the land. Since the loaves were once eatable everywhere, they are not considered 'limited to one place', so the 'all dwellings' rule cannot exclude them. That is why a separate verse was needed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This teaches': a new rule inferred from what was just said
Places where the משכן stood before the בית המקדש, when offerings could be eaten throughout the land

steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש is not saying these loaves may be eaten outside ירושלים today. He is saying that they were eatable everywhere in the נוב and גבעון period. Because of that, they are not in the category of 'food that cannot be eaten in all dwellings'.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
This teaches
phrases.notes: He derives a new rule from the fact that the simpler reason was not used.

are eaten in Nov and Givon.
phrases.notes: In that period they could be eaten anywhere in the land, so they count as eatable 'in all dwellings'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 and draws a new rule from it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Inference: the unused reason shows that the loaves really were eatable everywhere.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Offering loaves are limited to ירושלים, so the 'all dwellings' rule should exclude them.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the נוב and גבעון period these loaves could be eaten anywhere, so the 'all dwellings' rule does not exclude them. A special verse is needed.

steps.title: רבי אילעאי asks רבי אליעזר, who has no tradition
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי אילעאי asked רבי אליעזר whether one can fulfill the מצוה of מצה with חלות תודה or רקיקי נזיר. רבי אליעזר said he had not heard a ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אילעאי said, 'I asked רבי אליעזר: Can a person fulfill his obligation with thanksgiving loaves and נזיר wafers? He told me: I have not heard.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא on our topic. This step sets up the question, and the next step gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר was known for passing on only what he had received from his teachers. So 'I have not heard' means he had no tradition on this question. The question stays open for רבי יהושע to answer.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was taught': introduces a ברייתא
'What is the law: does one fulfill the obligation?'
'I have not heard': I have no tradition on this

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Ilai said:
I asked Rabbi Eliezer:
What is the law: may a person fulfill his obligation
with thanksgiving loaves and nazirite wafers?
He said to me: I have not heard.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעַאי: שָׁאַלְתִּי אֶת רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a ברייתא about the same loaves. It adds a distinction that our verses did not mention.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can one fulfill the מצוה of eating מצה with חלות תודה or רקיקי נזיר?

steps.title: רבי יהושע: For oneself, no; made for the market, yes
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע rules that loaves made for one's own offering do not work for the מצוה. Loaves baked to sell in the market do work.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I went and asked רבי יהושע. He told me: They said, thanksgiving loaves and נזיר wafers that a person made for himself cannot be used to fulfill the obligation. If he made them to sell in the market, he can fulfill it with them.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע answers the question. He divides the case by the baker's purpose: for his own offering, or for sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Loaves made for one's own offering are fully dedicated to the קרבן, so they are excluded, as the verses taught. Someone baking to sell has a different mindset. He knows he may not sell them and may end up eating them as מצה, so he bakes with that possibility in mind. רבה gives this reason in step 17.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They have already said': citing an earlier established teaching
'That he made for himself', for his own offering
'To sell in the market'

steps.whatToRemember: The loaves of רבה and רב יוסף's verses are excluded only when made for one's own offering. Loaves baked for sale in the market can be used for the מצוה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This narrows the earlier exclusion. The baker's purpose decides whether the loaves count as מצה for the מצוה.

phrases.english: I came and asked before Rabbi Yehoshua;
he said to me: They have said,
thanksgiving loaves and nazirite wafers
that he made for himself,
a person does not fulfill his obligation with them;
if made to sell in the market, he fulfills his obligation with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּאתִי וְשָׁאַלְתִּי לִפְנֵי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, אָמַר לִי: הֲרֵי אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question that רבי אליעזר could not answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Loaves made for one's own offering do not work for the מצוה. Loaves made for sale in the market do work.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: 'ברית! This is the tradition from סיני'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעאי reports רבי יהושע's ruling to רבי אליעזר. In the first version, רבי אליעזר excitedly swears that this is the very teaching given to משה at סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'When I came and told these things to רבי אליעזר, he said to me: By the covenant! These are the very words that were said to משה at סיני.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אילעאי brings the answer back to רבי אליעזר. In this version, רבי אליעזר strongly confirms that it is an authentic ancient tradition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ברית' is an oath, like saying 'I swear!'. Hearing the ruling reminded רבי אליעזר of a tradition going back to משה at סיני. So in this version, רבי יהושע's distinction is fully confirmed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And I laid out' or 'I recited' the words
'By the covenant!': an oath, like 'I swear!'
'Said to משה at סיני': an ancient, authoritative tradition

phrases.english: When I came and laid out these matters
before Rabbi Eliezer, he said to me:
By the covenant!
phrases.notes: An oath of excitement in this version.

phrases.english: These are the very words
that were said to Moses at Sinai.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁבָּאתִי וְהִרְצֵיתִי דְּבָרִים לִפְנֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי אליעזר's reaction confirms רבי יהושע's ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In this version, the distinction between loaves made for oneself and loaves made for the market is an ancient tradition from סיני.

steps.title: Second version: רבי אליעזר is astonished and asks for a reason
steps.stepSummary: In the איכא דאמרי version, רבי אליעזר's 'ברית!' is a cry of surprise. Is this really a tradition from סיני? Doesn't it need a reason?
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say he said: 'By the covenant! Are these really the words said to משה at סיני? Doesn't it need a reason?!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רבי אליעזר's reaction. Here he does not accept the ruling right away. He demands an explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same words are read as a surprised question instead of a statement. In this version, רבי יהושע's distinction does not come with a known tradition, so it needs logical support. This sets up the גמרא's next move: finding the reason for the market rule.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Some say': introduces an alternative version
'Doesn't it need a reason?!'

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'הן הן הדברים שנאמרו למשה בסיני' are the same in both versions. Only the tone changes. In version one it is an excited statement. In version two it is a doubtful question.

phrases.english: Some say:
By the covenant! Are these the very words
phrases.notes: Read here as a question of surprise.

phrases.english: that were said to Moses at Sinai?
Doesn't it need a reason?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: בְּרִית, הֵן הֵן הַדְּבָרִים שֶׁנֶּאֶמְרוּ לוֹ לְמֹשֶׁה בְּסִינַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is an alternative reading of the same reaction in step 14. It turns the confirmation into a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's distinction between loaves made for oneself and loaves made to sell in the market.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without a known tradition from סיני, a ruling that splits two similar cases must have a logical reason. Until one is given, the ruling is open to question.

steps.title: What is the reason for the difference?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why loaves made for one's own offering do not work for מצה, while loaves made for the market do.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the logic behind רבי יהושע's ruling. This short question sets up רבה's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע split the loaves into two groups but did not explain why. Both groups look the same: they are the same kind of loaves, baked for the same offerings. So the גמרא wants to know what makes the market loaves different.

keyTerms.meaning: Reason, logic
What?

phrases.english: And what is the reason?
phrases.notes: A short question. It asks for the logic behind רבי יהושע's split between one's own loaves and market loaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the איכא דאמרי version in step 15, which suggested the ruling must have a reason. The גמרא now asks directly what that reason is.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The logic that separates loaves baked for one's own תודה or נזיר offering from loaves baked to sell in the market.

steps.title: The market seller keeps the option of using them for מצה
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that a market seller thinks: 'If they sell, fine. If not, I will use them for my מצה.' So the מצוה was in his mind from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Whatever is made for the market, the seller keeps his options open. He says to himself: 'If it sells, it sells. If it doesn't sell, I will fulfill my obligation with it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the question. A seller is never sure his loaves will be bought, so he plans from the start that unsold loaves will be his own מצה for the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone baking loaves for his own offering has only the offering in mind. The מצוה of מצה is not part of his plan at all. The market seller is different. From the very beginning he keeps a backup plan to use the loaves for the מצוה. That makes his loaves fit for the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Market
He certainly keeps his options open (literally, 'he consults with himself / may change his mind')
It is sold
I will fulfill my obligation with them

steps.whatToRemember: Own-offering loaves: made only for the offering, so they do NOT work for מצה. Market loaves: the seller always had a backup plan to use them for the מצוה, so they DO work.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the market loaves are a different kind of bread. They are baked exactly the same way. The only difference is the baker's plan: the seller's plan included the מצוה of מצה from the start.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the baker's plan at the time of baking can decide whether מצה is fit for the מצוה.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
Anything made for the market, he keeps his options open.
phrases.notes: A seller is never certain his goods will be bought, so his plans stay flexible.

phrases.english: He says: if it is sold, it is sold;
phrases.notes: First option: someone buys the loaves for an offering.

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָא מִזְדַּבַּן — אִיפּוֹק בְּהוּ אֲנָא.
phrases.english: if it is not sold, I will fulfill my obligation with them.
phrases.notes: Backup option: the seller eats the unsold loaves as his מצה on פסח.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: כֹּל לַשּׁוּק אִימְּלוֹכֵי מִימְּלֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The market seller always plans that unsold loaves will be used for his own מצה. Because the מצוה of מצה is part of his plan from the start, his loaves qualify. The person baking for his own offering has no such plan.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Loaves baked for the market can be used for the מצוה of מצה because the seller keeps a backup plan to use them himself. Loaves baked for one's own offering cannot be used.
